statement: Keeping the linear action-value intercept constant improves learning useful food acquisition over full-vector L2 normalization at fixed features, reward and learner.
rationale: In the preceding learner all features, including the intercept, were divided by an action-dependent norm. A constant reward offset cannot then be represented by one bias coefficient; a large learned baseline may create spurious action preferences from feature magnitudes. A unit case proves the intercept varies between approaching/retreating an object. This algebraic issue motivates an empirical ablation, not a prior claim that it explains all failures.
falsification: No promotion unless a fixed-normalization learner passes every fixed criterion in all3 training seeds. Retain a partial lead only if hunger decreases>=.1 in>=2/3 seeds versus paired L2-lambda0 without aggregate thermal MAE, proximity or contact regression>10%. A normalization effect is assessed only in lambda0 pair; fixed lambda.9 separately tests traces. Final100k only; transient improvements cannot substitute for final policy.

sources.title: Original analysis of Live relational feature normalization
sources.mechanism: If x0=1/sqrt(sum_j x_j(a)^2), a change in other action features changes the intercept. Fixed x0=1 avoids this coupling.
sources.limitations: Fixed normalization changes the scale of non-intercept features and effective step sizes too. This pilot tests the complete normalization treatment; attribution solely to the intercept needs a further scale-matched ablation if promising.
